You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Diagnosis:
The test case `testLang294` is failing because it calls `StrBuilder.deleteAll("\n%BLAH%")` on a `StrBuilder` containing the string "\n%BLAH%\nDo more stuff\neven more stuff\n%BLAH%\n". The current bug report states that `StrBuilder.replaceAll` and `StrBuilder.deleteAll` can throw `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

From the `deleteAll` method implementation:
- It first calculates the length of the target string to delete.
- If the length is greater than 0, it finds the first index of the target using `indexOf`.
- It then enters a loop where it calls `deleteImpl` with the current index and deletes the substring of that length.
- It continues by looking for the next occurrence from the index of the last deletion.

The `deleteImpl` method shifts the internal buffer's content left by copying characters starting from `endIndex` to `startIndex` and reduces the size by the length of the deleted substring.

However, the problematic part arises when in the loop of `deleteAll`, after deleting at a certain index, the next `indexOf` search is restarted at the same index (which is where the deletion started). Since the buffer has shifted left, this can cause the `indexOf` to yield an incorrect index, possibly equal to the old buffer length, or cause the method to incorrectly state an index within size that leads to an out-of-bounds during subsequent array copy in `deleteImpl`.

Furthermore, looking at the `indexOf` method:
- It has a check for out-of-bound startIndex and returns -1 if out of range.
- But the for loop ends at `thisBuf.length - strLen`, where `thisBuf.length` is the full buffer length, which may not be equal to the logical size of the string (represented by `size`). This can cause incorrect index calculation where index is above the actual string size.

Therefore, the root cause seems to be:
1. In `deleteAll`, when searching for the next occurrence after deletion, it searches starting at the same index without advancing, which can cause infinite loops or out-of-bounds errors.
2. `indexOf` uses the full buffer length, not the current size of the string, in its loop bounds, causing it to read beyond the logical string boundaries.

In the test case the string contains multiple "\n%BLAH%" sequences, deleting them all triggers this bug.

The `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` in the bug report matches the symptoms of wrong buffer indexing during deletion due to these issues.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this problem.

Hence, this diagnosis is consistent with the failing test and the description given.

Next, I will identify the best methods to fix this bug.
org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.deleteAll(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.indexOf(java.lang.String,int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
